census_mfn_hs2.label: FTA/GSP preference utilization (HS2 x country)
census_mfn_hs2.detail: Share of this origin's HS2 imports that entered under a preferential program (FTA/GSP), from U.S. Census calculated-duty data. Weighted into the trade-weighted effective rate in pipeline step 6c (mfn_exemption_shares).

usmca_hts10.label: USMCA utilization (HTS10)
usmca_hts10.detail: Share entering under USMCA at the 10-digit level, from USITC DataWeb SPI ('S'/'S+') data. Applied to Canada/Mexico in pipeline step 7 (usmca_product_shares); more precise than the HS2-level preference weighting.

base_mfn_col1.narrative: Normal-trade-relations duty for {hts10} from {country_name}: {applied_pct} under HTSUS Column 1-General. No FTA/GSP preference reduces this origin's effective rate for this product.

base_free.narrative: {hts10} is Free (0%) under HTSUS Column 1-General; no MFN duty before additional Ch.99 programs.

base_col2.legal_authority: HTSUS Column 2 (Cuba, North Korea, Russia, Belarus)
base_col2.narrative: {country_name} is a non-NTR origin, so {hts10} dutiable at the Column 2 statutory rate ({applied_pct}).

base_special_usmca.legal_authority: USMCA (HTSUS General Note 11) or other special program
base_special_usmca.narrative: {hts10} from {country_name} enters Free under a special program (e.g. USMCA), overriding the Column 1-General rate.

base_mfn_blended.legal_authority: HTSUS Column 1-General, net of FTA/GSP preference utilization
base_mfn_blended.narrative: The base NTR/MFN (Column 1-General) rate for {hts10} is {statutory_pct}. About {preference_share_pct} of {country_name}'s trade in this category enters under an FTA/GSP preference program ({preference_source}), so the trade-weighted effective rate is {applied_pct}. A specific shipment owes the full base NTR/MFN rate unless it claims, and can substantiate, the applicable preference.

base_usmca_blended.legal_authority: USMCA Implementation Act (19 U.S.C. 4501 et seq.); HTSUS General Note 11, applied against the Column 1-General rate
base_usmca_blended.narrative: The base NTR/MFN (Column 1-General) rate for {hts10} is {statutory_pct}. About {preference_share_pct} of {country_name}'s trade in this 10-digit subheading enters duty-free under USMCA ({preference_source}), so the trade-weighted effective rate is {applied_pct}. A shipment that does not claim USMCA owes the full base NTR/MFN rate.

s232_steel.narrative: Section 232 steel duty {applied_pct} on {hts10} ({program_ch99}), per Proclamation 9705 as amended.

s232_steel_derivative.narrative: Section 232 steel-derivative duty on {hts10} ({program_ch99}): published rate {statutory_pct} applied to the DECLARED value of the steel content, not the full entered value. Computing duty owed requires the declared steel-content value.

s232_aluminum.narrative: Section 232 aluminum duty {applied_pct} on {hts10} ({program_ch99}), per Proclamation 9704 as amended.

s232_aluminum_derivative.narrative: Section 232 aluminum-derivative duty on {hts10} ({program_ch99}): published rate {statutory_pct} applied to the DECLARED value of the aluminum content, not the full entered value. Computing duty owed requires the declared aluminum-content value.

s232_copper.narrative: Section 232 copper duty {applied_pct} on {hts10} ({program_ch99}); applies to the copper content.

s232_copper_derivative.narrative: Section 232 copper-derivative duty on {hts10} ({program_ch99}): published rate {statutory_pct} applied to the DECLARED value of the copper content, not the full entered value. Computing duty owed requires the declared copper-content value.

s232_semiconductor.narrative: Section 232 semiconductor duty {applied_pct} on {hts10} ({program_ch99}), per U.S. Note 39.

s232_russia_proc10522.legal_authority: Proclamation 10522 (Feb 24, 2023), retained by the April 2026 proclamation
s232_russia_proc10522.narrative: Russia-origin {hts10} carries the flat 200% Section 232 metals rate under Proclamation 10522; this REPLACES the ordinary 232 base rate (it does not stack on it) and is continuous across 2023–2026.

s232_turkey_surtax.narrative: Turkey-origin steel {hts10} carried the elevated 50% Section 232 rate (Proclamation 9772, 2018–2019); a single-country override of the 25% blanket.

s232_usmca_exempt.legal_authority: April 2026 Section 232 annex, USMCA eligibility restoration
s232_usmca_exempt.narrative: {hts10} from {country_name} is USMCA-eligible and, post-April-2026 annex, restored to Section 232 exemption for annex auto/MHD products outside ch. 72/73/76. SAIL applies the exempt rate ({applied_pct}); without the USMCA claim, the {counterfactual_pct} Section 232 rate would apply instead.

s301_active.legal_authority: USTR China technology-transfer action; HTSUS notes 20/31 and headings 9903.88, 9903.91, 9903.92.10
s301_active.narrative: Section 301 China duty {applied_pct} on {hts10} ({program_ch99}), per the USTR action lists.

s301_exempt.narrative: The China technology-transfer charge is not applied to {hts10} from {country_name} in {revision}. Consult the source decision for the scope or exclusion basis; other Section 301 investigations require their own determination.

s301_scope_pending.legal_authority: Revision-specific HTSUS notes 20/31 and heading description
s301_scope_pending.narrative: Potential China technology-transfer duty on {hts10} ({program_ch99}); the preserved legal product description must be established before a shipment amount is known.

s301_maritime.legal_authority: USTR maritime action, note 31(k)-(l); FR 2025-19568 and suspension FR 2025-19873
s301_maritime.narrative: Potential maritime equipment duty on {hts10} ({program_ch99}); product description, Chinese origin/components/ownership, applicable claim and entry time require determination.

s301fl_active.legal_authority: USTR Section 301 forced-labor actions, 60 economies; U.S. note 52; HTSUS 9903.05.20-9903.05.84
s301fl_active.narrative: Section 301 forced-labor duty {applied_pct} on {hts10} ({program_ch99}) for {country_name}, per U.S. note 52 (eff. 2026-07-24).

s301br_active.legal_authority: USTR Section 301 Brazil action; U.S. note 50; HTSUS 9903.05.01
s301br_active.narrative: Section 301 Brazil duty {applied_pct} on {hts10} ({program_ch99}), per U.S. note 50 (eff. 2026-07-22).

ieepa_recip_active.narrative: IEEPA reciprocal surcharge {applied_pct} on {hts10} from {country_name} ({program_ch99}), per EO 14257.

ieepa_recip_floor.legal_authority: EO 14257; floor structure per FR 2025-23316 (90 FR 59281); 9903.02.xx
ieepa_recip_floor.narrative: {country_name}'s IEEPA reciprocal FLOOR ({program_ch99}) brings {hts10} up to {counterfactual_pct} when its Column 1-General rate ({base_pct}) is below the floor; SAIL applies {applied_pct} after stacking.

ieepa_exempt_annex_ii.legal_authority: U.S. Note 2(v)(iii) to subchapter III, ch. 99 (Annex II of EO 14257)
ieepa_exempt_annex_ii.narrative: {country_name}'s reciprocal program ({program_ch99}) would otherwise apply {counterfactual_pct} to {hts10} (its base rate {base_pct} is below the floor), but {hts10} is on the Annex II exemption ({authority}), which carves out of BOTH the baseline surcharge and the floor. SAIL applies the exempt rate ({applied_pct}); the exemption is claimed via {claimed_via}. If it is not claimed, the {counterfactual_pct} program rate applies instead (importer-non-claim exposure); so a $0 here is an intentional exemption, not a coverage gap.

ieepa_exempt_ita.legal_authority: U.S. Note 2(v)(iii) to subchapter III, ch. 99 (ITA-enumerated subheadings)
ieepa_exempt_ita.narrative: {hts10} is an ITA-enumerated semiconductor/electronics subheading on Annex II ({authority}), which carves out of the reciprocal program ({program_ch99}). SAIL applies the exempt rate ({applied_pct}); claimed via {claimed_via}. Unclaimed, the {counterfactual_pct} program rate would apply instead.

ieepa_exempt_ch98.narrative: {hts10} is a Chapter 98 provision statutorily exempt from the IEEPA reciprocal program ({authority}). SAIL applies the exempt rate ({applied_pct}); unclaimed, the {counterfactual_pct} program rate would apply instead.

ieepa_exempt_berman.legal_authority: Berman Amendment, 19 U.S.C. 2505 (Ch. 49 printed matter, Ch. 97 art/antiques)
ieepa_exempt_berman.narrative: {hts10} is informational material (Ch. 49 / Ch. 97) exempt from IEEPA under the Berman Amendment ({authority}). SAIL applies {applied_pct}.

ieepa_floor_exempt.narrative: {hts10} from {country_name} is on the floor-country product carve-out, so the {counterfactual_pct} reciprocal floor does not apply. SAIL applies {applied_pct}.

ieepa_country_eo_exempt.narrative: {hts10} from {country_name} is carved out of the country-specific IEEPA surcharge by the controlling executive order. SAIL applies the exempt rate ({applied_pct}); unclaimed, the {counterfactual_pct} surcharge would apply instead.

ieepa_duty_free_exempt.narrative: Under the active diagnostic scope, {hts10} (base {base_pct}, duty-free) is treated as exempt from the IEEPA reciprocal surcharge. SAIL applies {applied_pct}.

ieepa_not_in_program.short_label: Not applicable: origin not in reciprocal program
ieepa_not_in_program.narrative: {country_name} is not in the IEEPA reciprocal program for {revision}, so no reciprocal duty applies to {hts10}.

ieepa_fent_china.narrative: IEEPA fentanyl duty {applied_pct} on China-origin {hts10} ({program_ch99}), per EO 14195.

ieepa_fent_canada.narrative: IEEPA fentanyl/border duty {applied_pct} on Canada-origin {hts10} ({program_ch99}), per EO 14193.

ieepa_fent_mexico.narrative: IEEPA fentanyl/border duty {applied_pct} on Mexico-origin {hts10} ({program_ch99}), per EO 14194.

s201_solar.narrative: Section 201 solar safeguard {applied_pct} on {hts10} ({program_ch99}); Canada is USMCA-exempt from this safeguard.

gap_unresolved.narrative: No rate is joined to {hts10} for {country_name} in the loaded revision ({revision}). This is a genuine coverage gap; load the revision that covers this program before relying on this $0.

s232_basis_metal_content.legal_authority: Implementation of Duties on Aluminum (90 FR 11251, Mar 5, 2025) implementing Proclamation 10895; CSMS #65236645 (and successors)
s232_basis_metal_content.narrative: The Section 232 duty for {program_ch99} applies to the declared value of the {basis_metal} content, not the full entered value. CBP requires reporting the {basis_metal} content as a separate entry line (with content weight in kg) when its value is less than the total entered value; duties for required HTS reporting lines must not be combined onto one line. Computing duty owed requires the declared {basis_metal}-content value.

s232_full_value_proc11021.short_label: Duty basis: full entered value (Apr 6, 2026 framework)
s232_full_value_proc11021.legal_authority: Proclamation 11021 (91 FR 18201, Apr 9, 2026); Proclamation 11032 (Jun 2026 metals adjustment)
s232_full_value_proc11021.narrative: Under the April 6, 2026 metals framework, the Section 232 duty for {program_ch99} applies to the full customs value of the article (annex-tier treatment), superseding the earlier metal-content-value basis for derivative articles.

s122_non232_portion_only.short_label: Section 122 does not stack on the Section 232 portion
s122_non232_portion_only.legal_authority: Proclamation 11012 (91 FR 9339, Feb 25, 2026), Imposing a Temporary Import Surcharge; CBP CSMS guidance on Section 122 reporting
s122_non232_portion_only.narrative: The Section 122 surcharge does not apply in addition to Section 232 on the same value portion: where Section 232 applies to part of an import, Section 122 applies only to the part not subject to Section 232. It is not a blended or discounted rate — each portion carries its own published rate.

s232_full_value_no_content_split.short_label: Not owed: Section 232 covers the full value
s232_full_value_no_content_split.legal_authority: EO 14257 sec. 3(b) (reciprocal); EO 14289 sec. 3(a), 90 FR 18907, CBP CSMS #65054270 (non-stacking); Proclamation 11012 (91 FR 9339) (Section 122)
s232_full_value_no_content_split.narrative: This duty applies only to the part of an article's value that is not subject to Section 232. Section 232 applies to the full value of this article, so no part remains for this duty: it is replaced, not reduced. Where Section 232 applies to part of the value, this duty applies to the remainder.

s232_auto_parts_use_condition.short_label: Applies only to parts of passenger vehicles and light trucks
s232_auto_parts_use_condition.legal_authority: Proclamation 10908 (90 FR 14705); HTSUS chapter 99 U.S. note 33(f)-(h), headings 9903.94.05 and 9903.94.06
s232_auto_parts_use_condition.narrative: Heading 9903.94.05 applies the 25% duty only to parts of passenger vehicles (sedans, sport utility vehicles, crossover utility vehicles, minivans and cargo vans) and light trucks classified in a provision listed in U.S. note 33(g). An article in a listed provision that is not such a part reports under 9903.94.06 and owes no automobile-parts duty (note 33(h)(ii)); a USMCA-qualifying part also reports under 9903.94.06 (note 33(h)(i)). To decide, establish what the article is designed and sold for: the part number's vehicle application (make, model and fitment), the buyer and its use, and the product literature. If it is such a part: 25% under 9903.94.05, and the reciprocal and Section 122 duties do not apply to it. If not: 9903.94.06, no automobile-parts duty.

s232_semiconductor_criteria.short_label: Applies only to semiconductor articles meeting U.S. note 39's criteria
s232_semiconductor_criteria.legal_authority: Proclamation 11002 (91 FR 2443), effective January 15, 2026; HTSUS chapter 99 U.S. note 39(b), headings 9903.79.01-.09; CBP CSMS 67400472
s232_semiconductor_criteria.narrative: Heading 9903.79.01 applies the 25% duty only to a logic integrated circuit, or an article containing one, classified in 8471.50, 8471.80 or 8473.30, with either (1) total processing performance (TPP) above 14,000 and below 17,500 and total DRAM bandwidth above 4,500 GB/s and below 5,000 GB/s, or (2) TPP above 20,800 and below 21,100 and total DRAM bandwidth above 5,800 GB/s and below 6,200 GB/s (U.S. note 39(b)). To decide, check the product datasheet for TPP and DRAM bandwidth, then the end use: entries for U.S. data centers (over 100 MW of new AI load), repair or replacement, research and development, startups, consumer, civil industrial or public-sector use report under 9903.79.03-.09 at 0%. Meets the parameters with no exempt end use: 25% under 9903.79.01. Otherwise: 9903.79.02 (parameters not met) or the end-use heading, no Section 232 semiconductor duty.

proc10947_6_non_metal_content.short_label: Applies to the declared non-metal value of a Section 232 derivative
proc10947_6_non_metal_content.legal_authority: Proclamation 10947 of June 3, 2025, clause (6) (90 FR 24199); EO 14257 sec. 3(b); CBP CSMS 64348411, 65236374; copper: Proclamation 10962 clause (4), CSMS 65794272
proc10947_6_non_metal_content.narrative: From June 4, 2025 the non-steel, non-aluminum content of a Section 232 derivative article is subject to the reciprocal duty and any other applicable tariffs, reported on its own entry line; the metal content carries Section 232. Before June 4, 2025 the whole article was outside the reciprocal duty (EO 14257 sec. 3(b), heading 9903.01.33). The split needs the declared metal content value: when it is unknown, CBP collects Section 232 on the entire entered value on one line, and no non-metal portion remains for the reciprocal duty. The copper heading (9903.78.01) splits the same way from August 1, 2025.

ieepa_country_eo_active.short_label: Country-specific IEEPA duty (in addition to the reciprocal duty)
ieepa_country_eo_active.legal_authority: Brazil: EO 14323 (90 FR 37739), heading 9903.01.77, from Aug 6, 2025. India: EO 14329, heading 9903.01.84, from Aug 27, 2025
ieepa_country_eo_active.narrative: A country-specific IEEPA duty of {applied_pct} on {hts10} from {country_name} ({program_ch99}), owed in addition to the reciprocal duty and reported under its own heading.

in_transit_fentanyl_cn_2025_02.narrative: Goods loaded onto a vessel at the port of loading, or in transit on the final mode of transport, before 12:01 a.m. EST February 1, 2025 and entered before March 7, 2025 do not owe the 10% duty; they report under 9903.01.23. Verify the on-board date on the bill of lading. Otherwise the duty shown applies.

in_transit_reciprocal_2025_04_05.narrative: Goods loaded onto a vessel at the port of loading, or in transit on the final mode of transport, before 12:01 a.m. EDT April 5, 2025 and entered before May 27, 2025 owe no reciprocal duty; they report under 9903.01.28. Verify the on-board date on the bill of lading. Otherwise the duty shown applies.

in_transit_reciprocal_2025_04_09.narrative: Goods loaded before 12:01 a.m. EDT April 9, 2025 and entered before May 27, 2025 owe the 10% baseline under 9903.01.25 instead of the country rate. Verify the on-board date on the bill of lading. Otherwise the country rate shown applies.

in_transit_reciprocal_2025_08_07.narrative: Goods loaded before 12:01 a.m. EDT August 7, 2025 and entered before October 5, 2025 owe the 10% baseline under 9903.01.25 instead of the country rate. Verify the on-board date on the bill of lading. Otherwise the country rate shown applies.

in_transit_brazil_2025_08_06.narrative: Goods of Brazil loaded before 12:01 a.m. EDT August 6, 2025 and entered before October 5, 2025 do not owe the additional 40%; they report under 9903.01.78. Verify the on-board date on the bill of lading. Otherwise the duty shown applies.

in_transit_india_2025_08_27.legal_authority: EO 14329; CBP notice 90 FR 41837; CBP CSMS 66027027; heading 9903.01.85
in_transit_india_2025_08_27.narrative: Goods of India loaded before 12:01 a.m. EDT August 27, 2025 and entered before September 17, 2025 do not owe the additional 25%; they report under 9903.01.85. Verify the on-board date on the bill of lading. Otherwise the duty shown applies.

eo14289_3a_i_auto.short_label: Not owed: the Section 232 automobile duty takes precedence
eo14289_3a_i_auto.legal_authority: Executive Order 14289 of April 29, 2025, sec. 3(a)(i) (90 FR 18907)
eo14289_3a_i_auto.narrative: An article subject to the Section 232 automobile or automobile parts duty is not subject to the IEEPA Canada or Mexico duty, or to the Section 232 steel and aluminum duties.

eo14289_3a_ii_ieepa_camx.short_label: Not owed: the IEEPA Canada/Mexico duty takes precedence
eo14289_3a_ii_ieepa_camx.legal_authority: Executive Order 14289 of April 29, 2025, sec. 3(a)(ii) as originally issued (90 FR 18907); reversed from June 4, 2025 by Proclamation 10947 clause (5)
eo14289_3a_ii_ieepa_camx.narrative: Before June 4, 2025, an article subject to the IEEPA Canada or Mexico duty is not subject to the Section 232 steel and aluminum duties.

proc10947_5_metals.short_label: Not owed: the Section 232 steel/aluminum duty takes precedence
proc10947_5_metals.legal_authority: Proclamation 10947 of June 3, 2025, clause (5), amending EO 14289 sec. 3(a)(ii) (90 FR 24199), effective June 4, 2025
proc10947_5_metals.narrative: From June 4, 2025, an article subject to the Section 232 steel or aluminum duty is not subject to the IEEPA Canada or Mexico duty.

proc10962_5_auto.short_label: Not owed: the Section 232 automobile duty takes precedence over copper
proc10962_5_auto.legal_authority: Proclamation 10962 of July 30, 2025, clause (5) (90 FR 37727), effective August 1, 2025
proc10962_5_auto.narrative: An article subject to the Section 232 automobile or automobile parts duty is not subject to the Section 232 copper duty.

ieepa_terminated_eo14389.short_label: IEEPA tariffs ended for entries on/after Feb 24, 2026
ieepa_terminated_eo14389.legal_authority: EO 14389, Ending Certain Tariff Actions (91 FR 9347, Feb 25, 2026); CBP CSMS #67834313
ieepa_terminated_eo14389.narrative: IEEPA reciprocal and fentanyl/border tariffs are not collected for goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after February 24, 2026 (EO 14389; CBP CSMS #67834313). Entries before that date remain subject to the rates in effect at time of entry.

ieepa_india_headings_retired.narrative: Headings 9903.01.84–9903.01.89 are no longer in use for products of India entered on or after February 7, 2026 (CBP CSMS #67702087).

s232_basis_value_unknown_mode.short_label: Content value unknown: CBP may require full entered value
s232_basis_value_unknown_mode.legal_authority: CBP CSMS #65236645 (and successors) — UPDATED GUIDANCE: Import Duties on Imports of Aluminum and Aluminum Derivative Products
s232_basis_value_unknown_mode.narrative: If the metal-content value equals the entered value OR IS UNKNOWN, CBP requires reporting the Section 232 duty on the ENTIRE entered value on one entry summary line. If the content value is less than the entered value, the entry must be split into two lines (non-content portion and content portion, with content weight in kg). Do not compute a split-value duty stack until the importer provides a declared content value — confirm treatment with the broker/importer.
